questions.question_text: This question may have 1 or more options as correct answer. Please ensure to mark all correct options before submitting. Which ones from the following refers to the type of market?
questions.explanation: Types of Markets (by Goods Traded): Commodity Market (unbranded bulk goods), Stock Market (trading of company equity/services). Types of Markets (by Geography): Local, National, Global, International. All listed options (Commodity, Global, International, Stock) refer to types of markets.

questions.question_text: You visited the market to purchase a pair of shoes. Although the shoes fit your needs perfectly, you find them quite expensive. The seller is explaining all the features of the product, highlighting how they meet your needs and justifying the price. What is the seller attempting to do in this situation?

options.A: Create and justify value for the shoe in the mind of customer.
options.D: None of the given options are correct

questions.question_text: Raju feels deprived of having a vehicle for travelling within the city. It becomes extremely difficult for him many times to travel. He went out today and purchased a bike. In this case ____________ is can be said as his need and ___________ can be said as his want.
questions.explanation: Need: A felt sense of deprivation (e.g., need for a vehicle for traveling). Want: Specific satisfiers for needs (e.g., bike as a specific vehicle). In this case, Vehicle is the need (deprivation of transportation), and Bike is the want (specific satisfier for the vehicle need).

questions.question_text: "Rahul works in an ed-tech company. He went along with his team members to enquire for a Learning management System that acts as a platform for students to view the course content of the institute. They enquired and negotiated with a lot of vendors for a couple of days and then finalized the best one available in their budget." In this case, what kind of purchase is reflected?

Sagar is a successful entrepreneur. He buys a luxury watch that is marketed as a symbol of exclusivity and sophistication. This purchase enhances Sagar’s sense of self-worth and social status. Which type of need is being fulfilled in this case?
If a start-up company tries to generate a USP for it's offering, which of the following stages reflects this activity?
questions.explanation: Positioning refers to communication of USP (Unique Selling Proposition) to the customers. Positioning is the act of designing the company's offering and image to occupy a distinctive place in the mind of the target market. Generating a USP is a positioning activity, not segmentation or targeting.

questions.question_text: Segmentation is the process of dividing the _____________ market into _______________ groups.
Soham stores. targets only the children below 8 years for all types of items it has. What type of segmentation strategy can be seen in this case?
questions.explanation: Market Specialization: Serving many needs of a specific customer group (e.g., Selling stationary, books, and uniforms specifically to schools). Soham stores targets only children below 8 years for all types of items - this is Market Specialization, serving many needs of a specific customer group.

questions.question_text: This question may have one or multiple correct options as answers. STDP : Exclude the incorrect option and select all correct options.
questions.explanation: STDP framework: Segmentation (S) - Identifying the customer; Targeting (T) - Selecting the customer; Differentiation (D) - Distinguishing the offering from competitors; Positioning (P) - Creating a perception in the customer's mind. All are correct components of the STDP framework.

questions.question_text: Positioning is the process of selecting a homogeneous segmented part from the whole heterogeneous market to sell the product.
Differentiations related to form, features, performance, quality, etc. reflects ____________ differentiation.
___________ refers to communication of USP to the customers.
questions.explanation: Positioning refers to communication of USP (Unique Selling Proposition) to the customers. Positioning (Al Ries & Jack Trout): Positioning is not what you do to a product; it is what you do to the mind of the prospect. It's about creating a distinctive place in the customer's mind.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are the techniques of perceptual mapping?
Define the Market Sizes: Potential Market, Available Market, and Target Market.

options.A: Bottom: Potential Market (interest), Middle: Available Market (interest, income, access), Top: Target Market (pursued part).
options.B: Top: Potential Market (interest), Middle: Available Market (interest, income, access), Bottom: Target Market (pursued part).
options.C: Bottom: Target Market (pursued part), Middle: Available Market (interest, income, access), Top: Potential Market (interest).
options.D: Bottom: Available Market (interest, income, access), Middle: Potential Market (interest), Top: Target Market (pursued part).

questions.question_text: Which of the following reflects different forms of competition?
Mark all options reflecting purchase intention categories.
questions.explanation: Purchase Intention Categories: Firm Immediate (ready to buy now), Firm Not Immediate (intend to buy but not immediately), Not Interested (neutral/no intention), Negative (actively avoiding purchase). All listed options reflect purchase intention categories used to classify consumer readiness to purchase.

questions.question_text: Which type of problem solving, customer will normally be very comfortable as he knows almost everything.
Which of the following categories will finally lead to either the selection ot rejection the product/brand in wishlist.
questions.explanation: The Evoked (Consideration) Set is the shortlist of brands considered for purchase. Brands in this set are seriously considered and will finally lead to either the selection or rejection of the product/brand in wishlist. Inept Set includes rejected brands, Inert Set includes indifferent brands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following will lead to customer satisfaction?
__________ reflects tha way, the person interacts with the environment.
questions.explanation: Personality reflects the way the person interacts with the environment. Personality: Inner psychological characteristics (e.g., aggressive, introverted). It is an Internal (Psychological) Factor that influences consumer behavior, along with Motivation, Perception, Learning, and Attitude.

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of B2B marketing according to the transcript?

options.C: To develop customers who will stay with you

questions.explanation: The primary objective of B2B marketing is to develop customers who will stay with you. B2B markets focus on long-term relationships (partnerships) rather than single transactions. Relationship Marketing focuses on customer retention and long-term engagement rather than transactional sales.

questions.question_text: Which type of buyer is characterized by a focus on price and sees products as commodities?
questions.explanation: Commodity Buyers: View products as undifferentiated. Focus: Price. Force vendors to strip value-added services. Strategy: Only serve if you have high volume/scale economy. They see products as commodities and focus primarily on price rather than value-added services.

questions.question_text: Why are underperformers considered risky customers for suppliers?

options.B: They operate in industries with high fixed costs
options.C: They are loyal and offer consistent orders

questions.explanation: Underperformers: Industries with high fixed costs (e.g., Steel, Pharma). Demand free services/low price; not loyal. Strategy: Avoid. They consume resources without profitability. They operate in industries with high fixed costs, making them risky and unprofitable for suppliers.

questions.question_text: What defines the most valuable customers in a B2B context?

options.B: They often switch suppliers for better deals
options.C: They invest in the supplier's business to improve outcomes
options.D: They prefer standardized products over customized solutions

questions.question_text: Which market consists of institutions like schools and hospitals, characterized by low budgets and captive clientele?
questions.explanation: Institutional Markets: Schools, Hospitals, Prisons. Characteristics: Low budgets, captive clientele. Strategy: Cost minimization (L1 bidder usually wins). They are characterized by low budgets and captive clientele, making price the primary decision factor.

questions.question_text: What is the primary focus during the introduction stage of the product life cycle?
In service management, what is meant by "service quality"?

options.C: The overall experience and satisfaction of the customer

questions.explanation: Service Quality is the overall experience and satisfaction of the customer. It encompasses all aspects of the service encounter including reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy, and tangibles. The primary objective of service quality management is enhancing customer satisfaction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a component of the product life cycle?
In product line management, what is meant by "line filling"?

options.A: Adding new products to the line
options.B: Introducing more items within the existing range
options.D: Reducing the number of product variations

questions.explanation: Line Filling: Adding more items within the present range to plug gaps and keep competitors out. This is different from Line Stretching (lengthening beyond current range), Line Pruning (removing unprofitable products), or Line Modernization (updating style/technology).

questions.question_text: What is a primary objective of service quality management?
questions.explanation: The primary objective of service quality management is enhancing customer satisfaction. Service Quality is the overall experience and satisfaction of the customer. While standardization and cost reduction may be supporting objectives, the primary focus is on customer satisfaction.

questions.question_text: How does understanding the characteristics of retailing influence a company's pricing strategy?

options.A: It allows for uniform pricing across all markets.
options.B: It enables tailoring pricing to match customer expectations and shopping behavior.
options.C: It eliminates the need for market research.
options.D: It focuses solely on production costs without considering customer insights.

questions.question_text: What is a primary goal of distribution channels in retailing?

options.D: To ensure products reach the end customer efficiently

questions.explanation: A primary goal of distribution channels in retailing is to ensure products reach the end customer efficiently. Distribution channels (Place in 4Ps) are about Delivering Value - getting products to customers through appropriate channels (Level 0: Direct, Level 1: Retailer, Level 2: Wholesaler-Retailer, etc.).

questions.question_text: In pricing strategies, what does price discrimination involve?

options.A: Offering the same price to all customers
options.B: Charging different prices to different customers based on willingness to pay
options.D: Setting prices based on production costs alone

questions.explanation: Price Discrimination: Charging different prices for the same product based on Customer Segment (Student/Senior citizen discounts), Time (Peak vs. Off-peak), Location (Airport vs. Supermarket), or Channel (Online vs. Offline). It involves charging different prices to different customers based on willingness to pay.

questions.question_text: When conducting a channel analysis, which of the following factors is least likely to impact the effectiveness of a distribution strategy?
questions.explanation: Channel analysis factors include: Customer accessibility, Channel performance metrics, Market coverage and penetration, Channel member selection (financial strength, reputation, service capability). Historical advertising campaigns are promotional activities (Promotion in 4Ps), not directly related to distribution channel effectiveness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between pricing strategies and customer satisfaction?

options.A: Higher prices always lead to higher customer satisfaction.
options.B: Effective pricing strategies can enhance perceived value and improve customer satisfaction.
options.C: Pricing strategies should be independent of customer feedback.
options.D: Price reductions guarantee an increase in customer loyalty.

questions.explanation: Effective pricing strategies can enhance perceived value and improve customer satisfaction. Perceived Value = What the customer thinks the product is worth. When pricing aligns with perceived value and customer expectations, it enhances satisfaction. Value = Benefit divided by Cost.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key objective of promotional strategies in marketing?
In the B2B sales process, which step involves understanding the specific needs of a potential client?
questions.explanation: Sales Process Steps: 1) Prospecting (identifying potential customers), 2) Pre-approach (researching prospect before contact - needs, habits, preferences), 3) Approach, 4) Presentation & Demonstration, 5) Handling Objections, 6) Closing, 7) Follow-up. Needs assessment involves understanding the specific needs of a potential client.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of personal selling in marketing?

options.B: To build direct relationships and tailor solutions to customer needs

questions.explanation: Personal Selling: Face-to-face interaction with prospective buyers. Characteristics: Customized, relationship-oriented, immediate feedback. Best for complex/B2B products. Purpose: To build direct relationships and tailor solutions to customer needs. It's about customization and relationship building, not automation.

questions.question_text: What is the primary role of budgeting in marketing campaigns?

options.A: To set and allocate financial resources for marketing activities

questions.explanation: The primary role of budgeting in marketing campaigns is to set and allocate financial resources for marketing activities. Budgeting methods include: Affordable Method, Percentage of Sales, Competitive Parity, and Objective and Task Method (most scientific - defines goal, determines tasks, estimates costs).
